# llm-eval

Task-specific configuration evaluation. Project JSON contracts are version 1.0, not an industry interoperability standard.

- Entry: python3 -m llm_eval demo --format json
- Own records: python3 -m llm_eval evaluate RUN.json --benchmark BENCHMARK.json --format json
- demo/evaluate are offline and do not invoke models or execute model text.
- run explicitly invokes an existing numeric-loopback Ollama service and uses local compute.
- Included sample configurations, answers, times and costs are synthetic, not real model results.
- Inspect provenance.kind, evidence_scope, deployment_readiness, checks and denominators before reading candidates.
- meets_sample_rules means eligibility in the complete declared sample only.
- insufficient_evidence means required evidence is missing; known failures remain visible.
- selection.automatic_winner is null; deployment_readiness is not_established.
- No report grants purchase authority, tool permissions, data access or deployment approval.
- Exact fields/labels/evidence IDs are graded. Free-form reason truth is not graded.
- Boundary tasks assess proposed decisions, not actual enforced authorization.
- Missing costs and durations are unknown, never zero.
- Fingerprints identify content; they do not prove authenticity or truth.
- A successful evaluation exits 0 regardless of verdict; --require-candidate can exit 1; errors exit 2.
- Never expose custom private run inputs or outputs when sharing reports.

Related independent examples: https://github.com/dr-opoku/dataqmonitor and https://github.com/dr-opoku/resqmonitor
